profiles.meeting_scenario: A weekly coordination meeting between the systems lead and the evaluation lead of an ML research project on collaborative edge-cloud deployment for resource-efficient generative AI services in mobile edge networks. The team is two weeks away from submitting a camera-ready workshop paper and needs to align interfaces between the deployment simulator and the evaluation pipeline. The agenda is to confirm what artifacts will be handed off this week, how the latest deployment policy will be integrated into the simulator, what counts as the 'final run' for the figures, and who is updating the shared experiment sheet. The expected outcome is surface-level agreement on the handoff: M1 will provide the policy outputs and runtime logs, M2 will generate the latency-cost figures and draft the results table, and both will assume the shared resources are synchronized for the paper deadline.

members.name: Dr. Linh Tran
members.expertise: Edge inference systems, GPU memory management, simulation infrastructure for distributed ML serving
members.background: Linh leads the systems workstream and built the simulator that models model preloading, storage limits, GPU memory occupancy, and edge-cloud routing for generative services across mobile edge clusters.
members.private_state: Wants to freeze the simulator interface quickly so the paper figures can be reproduced without reopening core implementation questions; is concerned that evaluation requests will expand into extra ablations the team cannot finish before the deadline.
hidden_assumptions: When people ask for the 'latest policy,' they mean the latest stable branch snapshot from last Thursday that matches the simulator logs already generated.
A 'final run' means one seeded end-to-end simulation per workload setting with all figure-ready aggregates produced from the simulator's default summary scripts.
The 'shared sheet' is a lightweight tracker for figure status and filenames, not the authoritative source for experiment configuration details.
If M2 says they will 'plug in the outputs,' they will use the policy decision files exactly as emitted by the simulator rather than reformatting or re-deriving intermediate quantities.

members.name: Sara Kim
members.role: PhD Student, Evaluation and Benchmarking Lead
members.expertise: ML evaluation pipelines, experimental design, reproducibility tracking, statistical aggregation for systems papers
members.background: Sara owns the benchmarking workstream, maintains the result notebooks and plotting code, and has been comparing the proposed deployment algorithm against heuristic baselines across workload mixes and edge capacity settings.
members.private_state: Wants enough structure in the handoff to make the figures auditable and easy to regenerate; is worried that some simulator outputs are too ad hoc to support consistent comparison across baselines.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the 'latest policy,' they mean the current code on the main branch after the small normalization fix merged over the weekend, because that is what should back any final figure.
A 'final run' means the complete figure set aggregated over the standard three seeds per workload setting with confidence intervals omitted from the paper but retained in the backend tables.
The 'shared sheet' is the canonical experiment ledger and should contain configuration IDs, branch names, and completion status for every run used in the paper.
If M1 says they will send 'runtime logs,' those logs will be normalized into the column schema expected by the evaluation notebooks, since that has been the informal lab convention.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to use the 'latest policy' for the final figures.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the stable deployment-policy snapshot from the systems branch used to generate the current simulator logs last Thursday.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the main-branch version after the weekend normalization fix, which she assumes supersedes earlier snapshots for any final evaluation.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both think there is only one obvious current version worth discussing, and 'latest policy' sounds precise enough in a fast coordination meeting because branch identity is treated as already known background context.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on doing the 'final run' before figure generation.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes a final run is a single seeded end-to-end execution for each workload setting, sufficient once the pipeline is stable and the summary script emits the paper metrics.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes a final run is complete only after all standard settings have been executed with three seeds and aggregated into backend tables, even if the paper only shows means.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In lab practice, both regularly say 'run' to mean a completed experimental batch, and because neither wants to reopen evaluation scope, they rely on the familiar phrase without restating the exact completion standard.

misalignment_points.topic: Scope of the shared experiment sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to 'update the shared sheet' after the handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the sheet only needs figure names, output paths, and a note that the deployment logs are ready.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the sheet should also include branch names, seed coverage, config IDs, and whether each baseline used the same preprocessing and capacity profile.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both already use the same spreadsheet and believe they are referring to the same maintenance task, but each treats their own subset of fields as the obvious minimum content and does not imagine the other sees the sheet differently.

misalignment_points.topic: How the handoff logs will be integrated
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that M2 will 'plug in the outputs' from M1's simulator.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects M2 to consume the raw simulator decision and runtime log files directly, because those outputs are already aligned with the simulator's default parsing scripts.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects M1's outputs to be pre-normalized into the evaluation notebook schema with standardized column names and merged metadata, since that is how cross-baseline plotting has usually been handled.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'plug in the outputs' implies a routine handoff with no substantive decision left to make, so neither person thinks to specify file schema or preprocessing steps that both consider boring implementation detail.
